args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. The deployment history shows v2.3.1 and v2.3.1-rc both as unhealthy. The most recent healthy release was v2.3.0. I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions. After the rollback, the service reports healthy on v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is passing health checks again.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, is also marked unhealthy in the release history.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy release, so I rolled back to that. It's now running in all three regions and the error rate is down to 0.2%. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had already run healthy in production.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2) describes the failure, the rollback and the result, and has paged the on-call engineer.

v2.3.1 shouldn't be redeployed until someone finds out why it broke.
